newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher in active trade.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Tuesday in active trading following the rise of Israeli shares traded in New York and the successful offering of Israel Discount Bank, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.62 percent, or 1.59 points, to 256.95 on an all-share turnover of 120 million shekels against 97 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.61 percent higher at 266.57.

"The market was showing strength today. The main reason for today's rise was the successful offering of Israel Discount Bank. This is a clear indication that the primary market is recovering," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.
The offering of Israel Discount Bank shares and warrants was three times oversubscribed and the price closed on Monday at nine percent above the minimum.

The government raised 170 million shekels from the public offering and 42 million shekels from an issue to the bank's workers. It expects to raise another 171 million shekels from the warrants exercised in July and 238 million shekels in November.
Israel Discount Bank, the most active share on Tuesday, gained 1.75 percent to 349 agorot on high volume of 28 million shekels.

"The offering is a good sign. The market was also reacting to the rise of Israeli shares traded on Wall Street and to the talks about the possibility of a unity government," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.

Traders said the market was indifferent to the release of the March consumer price index (CPI). "The fact that volume was relatively high shows that investors pay no attention to the inflation figure," Tsur said.
The CPI, released after the end of the trading day, rose 1.0 percent. The figure was above analysts' expectations of a 0.7-0.8 percent rise.

Other active shares included Koor Industries, which rose 2.0 percent to 30,573 agorot on volume of 8.7 million and Discount Investment Corp, which fell 1.75 percent to 25,669 on turnover of 4.6 million shekels.
